system_description.narrative_title: Nvidia CEO scandal triggers US-China chip-security showdown
system_description.narrative_summary: A newly revealed affair between Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy has precipitated his resignation and a board leadership crisis, sparking market turmoil and an executive succession scramble. The scandal has amplified bipartisan pressure in Washington to tighten export controls, drawn scrutiny of third‑party dealers (Megaspeed, Singapore intermediaries) and Commerce Department decisions, and threatens to reshape global AI chip flows and investor confidence.
system_description.scope: Events, actors and processes directly tied to the Jensen Huang affair and resignation: Nvidia's leadership and board decisions, employee relations and internal probe, US investigations and congressional action on chip exports, third‑party customers and re‑export channels (Megaspeed, Singapore links), market reactions and legal/regulatory follow‑ups.
system_description.super_system: Global AI–semiconductor–national security system (the US‑China technology rivalry and global supply chains)
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and AI investment ecosystem
US political and regulatory apparatus (Congress, Commerce, DOJ)
China's AI industry and procurement networks
International re‑export and intermediary trade networks (Singapore, third‑party dealers)
evidence_headlines: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns, in blow to AI boom he helped foster
Nvidia’s Jensen Huang admits to affair after allegations of relationship with Chinese spy
Speaker Johnson says Congress developing consensus on limiting chip exports to China
Megaspeed's links to rural Australian store raise fresh questions in Nvidia scandal
Singapore barred Alice Huang from re-entry following investigation
Lutnick faces questions over Nvidia spy scandal. His sons’ firm has deep ties to the chipmaker

variables.name: Leadership stability
variables.description: The overall continuity and steadiness of executive-level decision-making authority within the firm-related organizational node.

variables.name: Board cohesion
variables.description: The degree of alignment and coordinated action among board members when making governance and oversight decisions.

variables.name: Executive succession readiness
variables.description: The preparedness and availability of qualified internal or near-internal candidates and processes to replace senior executives smoothly.

variables.name: Internal probe intensity
variables.description: The pace and thoroughness of ongoing internal fact‑finding, disciplinary, and compliance investigation activities.

variables.name: Regulatory pressure intensity
variables.description: The level of external political and regulatory advocacy pushing for tighter oversight or restrictions related to technology transfer and corporate conduct.

variables.name: Export control stringency
variables.description: The strictness and enforceability of controls governing cross‑border transfers of advanced semiconductor technologies and related items.

variables.name: Third‑party intermediary opacity
variables.description: The obscurity and traceability gap in sales, distribution, and resale channels operated by intermediaries and dealers.

variables.name: Re‑export leakage risk
variables.description: The probability and expected rate at which controlled or sensitive hardware is diverted through secondary markets or re‑exports to restricted end destinations.

variables.name: Advanced chip cross‑border flow rate
variables.description: The volume-per-time of advanced AI/semiconductor hardware moving across international boundaries through all channels.

variables.name: Investor confidence in AI assets
variables.description: The aggregate market sentiment and willingness of investors to commit capital to firms and projects tied to advanced AI semiconductors.

variables.name: Market price volatility
variables.description: The short‑term fluctuation intensity in equity and financing valuations of firms linked to advanced AI semiconductor supply and demand.

variables.name: Legal and litigation exposure
variables.description: The accumulated likelihood and potential magnitude of legal claims, regulatory sanctions, and civil liabilities arising from corporate conduct or disclosures.

variables.name: Supply‑chain resilience
variables.description: The capacity of the semiconductor and AI hardware supply network to absorb disruptions and continue delivering critical inputs on schedule.

variables.name: Corporate reputation damage
variables.description: The cumulative erosion of trust and public standing of the organizational node among customers, partners, regulators, and the public.

variables.name: Legislative and congressional scrutiny
variables.description: The intensity and frequency of formal legislative inquiries, hearings, and oversight actions focused on technology transfer and related corporate behavior.

variables.name: Geopolitical tech‑access tension
variables.description: The ambient level of interstate strategic tension and policy friction specifically concerning access to advanced technologies and supply chains.

catalysts.title: Congressional hearings and inquiries into Nvidia and Commerce
catalysts.description: Formal hearings, subpoenas and record-preservation requests by House and Senate committees into the Huang affair, Nvidia exports and Commerce Dept. actions.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple headlines: calls for testimony/subpoenas, senators urging preservation, Congress developing consensus on limits.

catalysts.title: Push to tighten U.S. export controls on advanced chips
catalysts.description: Legislative and executive momentum toward stricter controls on Nvidia-class chip exports to China, including possible new rules or enforcement actions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Congress developing consensus to limit chip exports; explainers say tougher curbs likely after resignation.

catalysts.title: Nvidia internal probe led by outside counsel
catalysts.description: Wachtell/Paul Weiss-led internal investigation into Huang's conduct and related export/sales practices, producing findings and possible referrals.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: Nvidia hires former US prosecutor / Paul Weiss to lead probe; board meeting to decide Huang's future.

catalysts.title: Malaysia probe into possible re‑exports tied to Megaspeed
catalysts.description: Malaysian authorities investigate whether Nvidia-powered chips linked to Megaspeed were re‑exported to restricted destinations.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: Malaysia probing whether chips linked to Megaspeed unit were re‑exported.

catalysts.title: Possible Huang stock sales / wealth transfers
catalysts.description: Potential large-scale sales or transfers of Jensen Huang’s and family-held Nvidia stock that could pressure markets and ownership dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: Headline questions whether Huang will sell his $135bn of stock; family control complicates aftermath.

catalysts.title: Search and appointment of Nvidia permanent CEO
catalysts.description: Board process to appoint a permanent CEO (internal or external), including approaches to candidates such as Arm's Haas.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Nvidia has begun search, approached Arm CEO Haas; board has not selected search firm yet.

catalysts.title: US‑China tech access tensions and diplomatic responses
catalysts.description: Diplomatic exchanges and retaliatory rhetoric/steps between Washington and Beijing over use of the scandal to justify tech curbs.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: China warns against using scandal as pretext; warnings of trade frictions and blocking Beijing's access.

catalysts.title: Commerce Secretary Lutnick testimony and job risk
catalysts.description: Expected congressional testimony and mounting pressure on Commerce Secretary Lutnick, including talk of removal by the White House.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Lutnick faces questions, reportedly will testify; White House weighing his ouster amid fallout.
